scenario: AITA for not forgiving my younger sister? | My sister is very nice sometimes. But she's also very annoying and rude at other times. Something that's been pissing me off lately is the fact that she never focuses with me. Wheather I am telling her a story, or showing her something, or teaching her something, she doesn't focus. She claims she is focusing with me with her ears and understands perfectly. I always tell her that it annoys me when she does that because I feel like she isn't focusing. For a while now, I've been teaching her to play songs on the guitar. This is the best way we bond and I really enjoy it. The only problem is that she only focuses with her ears and not her eyes, that way, I can't tell the difference between "I can hear and understand you" and "I wasn't focusing". So I politely ask her to stop. Eventually (as usual) I lose my temper and yell like a school teacher to her loud students. She apologises and everything is fine. But that's not the problem. A while ago, I did something I was really proud of. I went to the living room to show my sister and she was only focusing with her hearing (I was playing guitar). I understood that she was focusing with me because it happens a lot. But I soon realized she was looking at the computer we share. I lost my temper and left before I can finish what I wanted to show her. She apologized and I didn't forgive her. I am planning to forgive her once I post this text, but I just wanted to know if I was the A-hole.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the "A-hole" in this situation with my younger sister. Let me start by understanding what an "A-hole" means. From what I know, it's slang for someone who is acting like a jerk or being unreasonable. So, the question is, did I act like a jerk when I didn't forgive my sister after she wasn't paying attention to me while I was showing her something on the guitar? Alright, let's break down the situation. My sister can be nice sometimes, but she's also annoying and rude at other times. One thing that's been bothering me is that she doesn't focus when I'm talking to her, teaching her something, or showing her something. She claims she's focusing with her ears and understands perfectly, but I feel like she's not really paying attention. This has been a recurring issue, especially when I'm teaching her to play songs on the guitar, which is something we both enjoy and a good way for us to bond. The problem arises because she only focuses with her ears and not with her eyes. This makes it hard for me to tell if she's actually paying attention or just pretending to listen. I've politely asked her to stop this behavior, but as usual, I lose my temper and yell at her like a strict teacher. She apologizes, and everything seems fine, but that's not the main issue here. A while ago, I did something I was really proud of and wanted to show it to my sister. I went to the living room, and she was on our shared computer. I assumed she was focusing on me because she was listening to me play the guitar, but then I realized she was actually looking at the computer. This made me lose my temper, and I left before I could finish showing her what I was proud of. She apologized, but I didn't forgive her. Now, I'm planning to forgive her once I post this text, but I want to know if I was the "A-hole" in this situation. So, was I being unreasonable? Let's think about this. I was teaching her something we both enjoy, and she wasn't giving me her full attention. I asked her to stop, but I ended up losing my temper. She apologized, but I held a grudge. Is it wrong to hold onto that anger, or is it justified because she wasn't respecting my time and effort? On one hand, I understand that she might not always be fully attentive, and maybe she didn't realize she was being disrespectful. On the other hand, I was trying to share something important with her, and her lack of attention was frustrating. It's also possible that I overreacted by losing my temper and not giving her the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps I should consider her perspective. Maybe she was trying to listen but found it hard to focus, or perhaps she was dealing with something else on the computer. It's also possible that she didn't realize I was upset until I yelled at her. In that case, my reaction might have been more about my own frustration than her actual behavior. Additionally, holding onto anger and not forgiving her might not be healthy for our relationship. Forgiveness is important, and it allows both parties to move forward without lingering resentment. By planning to forgive her after posting this, I'm taking a step towards resolving the issue, but I still need to reflect on whether my initial reaction was justified or if I was being too harsh. In summary, while I was frustrated with her lack of attention and felt disrespected, losing my temper and not forgiving her might have been an overreaction. It's important to communicate my feelings calmly and give her the chance to understand and make amends. Forgiveness helps maintain a healthy relationship and allows both of us to grow from the experience.
